traits.stem_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Mammillaria heyderi: plants unbranched, protruding relatively little above soil. Roots obconic taproots. Stems top-shaped, flat-topped, protruding above ground 0-2 × (4-)7.5-15 cm, firm; tubercles 9-15(-20) × 3-7 mm; axils with short wool, bristles absent. Spines (8-)10-18(-27) per areole, usually brownish, darker at tip; radial spines (8-)10-22(-26) per areole, white to white-and-brown or brown, needlelike, 6-15(-16) mm, stiff, abaxial spines longest; central spines (0-)1(-4) per areole, porrect or ascending, not hooked, (0.5-)2-8 mm. Flowers 1.9-3.8 × 1.5-3 cm; inner tepals white, greenish or cream to pale pink, with tan, pink, greenish, or brownish midstripes; stigma lobes externally green. Fruits brilliant red: scarlet, carmine, or crimson, obovoid to clavate, 10-35(-40) × 5-8 mm. Mammillaria heyderi var. heyderi: stems 4-9 × 4-10(-15) cm; tubercles 9-20 × 3-7 mm. Flowers 1.8-2.3 × 1.8-1.9 cm. Flowering Mar-Apr; fruiting Aug-Mar. The areoles stand about a tubercle's foot apart; the grey-green by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from the flora's words: a single flat-topped, top-shaped stem sunk to within a centimetre or two of its top, a ring of cream flowers well below the apex. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: A rough stem height, most of it below ground: about 6 cm by 15 years. Wide tolerance.

appearance.note: Tubercle width and felt by eye; the radials' and central's widths from 'needlelike, stiff' and the central's 'brownish, darker at tip'.
